university.title: University
university.preview: The very first lines of code.
university.memory: The first time a tiny project finally worked, I couldn't stop clicking through it. I thought I was pretty good — until I stepped into the real world.
university.story: I started engineering with circuits and electrical calculations. But wait, why wasn't it as fun as writing HTML and CSS? Maybe it was time to give web development a proper try.
highlights: Started with simple HTML, CSS, and JavaScript.
Connected a database with PHP in class, then built on it for my final-year project.
Interned at a software house (Node.js + Express, Nuxt 3 + TypeScript).
university.takeaway: Time to step into the real world of work.

career.title: First Job / Present
career.shortDescription: From my first job to everyday building and learning.
career.description: Turning ideas into real-world applications, while building, learning, and exploring new technologies.
career.preview: From my first job to the work I do today.
career.memory: A teammate's small suggestion during a code review solved a problem I'd been staring at all afternoon. Building together changed how I learned.
career.story: My first job became a place to keep growing. The same journey now includes taking ideas from a sketch to a working application and improving them with a team.
highlights: Built interfaces and connected them to application services.
Learned through code reviews, releases, and user feedback.
Kept exploring mobile apps, hardware, and side projects.
career.takeaway: Good software grows through collaboration and steady improvements.

first.title: First Job
first.description: From a class project to code my teammates would have to read.
first.story: On day one, the repo looked completely unfamiliar. Even getting it running meant asking lots of questions. My first task was a small form fix, but getting through the review taught me much more than I expected.
highlights: Mission 01: Get the project running. Everything else can wait.
Mission 02: Fix a form, connect an API, and open my first pull request.
Mission 03: Apply the feedback and hold my breath during the release.
first.memory: I thought working code meant I was done… until a teammate asked, “What if the API goes down?” Right. There was a lot more to think about.
first.takeaway: Make it work, then learn to make it understandable to someone else.

present.title: What am I tinkering with now?
present.description: Day job, side ideas, and a workbench that is getting a little crowded.
present.story: Some days I build an app. Other days I wire a circuit or watch the printer work. Not everything gets finished, but every experiment teaches me something new.
highlights: Connect frontend features with backend services.
Improve existing flows using feedback and small experiments.
present.memory: What if a mobile app controlled a board inside a case I printed myself? No idea what I would use it for yet, but it sounds fun to try.
present.takeaway: Get one idea working first. There will always be another one to try.
present.storyTitle: There is more to try beyond the screen

future.story: A new app? Something I can hold in my hands? Or something I have not even imagined yet? No idea, but there must be plenty left to try.
highlights: Prototype a small app that solves an everyday problem.
Combine a connected device with a custom printed enclosure.
Share an experiment and learn from the people who try it.
